DROPPER: full playtest report

A detailed mobile playtest of DROPPER: 15 bugs sorted by priority, suggestions, FTUE, bosses, progression times and my final verdict. Tap a section to open it.

🐞 Bugs15 found: 11 minor, 1 moderate, 3 major

MinorLowest priority, only affects the game slightly.

Tutorial timing. The tutorial asks you to press time stop while its cooldown hasn't finished. By the time it's ready you're already close to the obstacle, so it's safer to just dodge normally than risk it.

Slow start. Sometimes a stage starts a few seconds late. It happened on multiple maps.

Pause message overlap. In boss fights the health bar covers the pause message on mobile.

Enlarged aim box. On the first level of Fairy Ring the aim box gets bigger, which makes clearing obstacles harder.

Console warning. On joining, the console shows a warning about Roblox's core GUI.

Message covers a button. In phase 2 of the Fairy Ring boss, the “she is furious” message almost completely covers the time stop button, so you can't use it.

Black screen. If you suddenly leave a map, the main screen turns black and the buttons look a bit broken.

Music overlap. The up arrow button overlaps the name of the song that's playing.

Text hidden by Roblox UI. The “every server, every runner” text is covered by Roblox's own buttons on mobile.

Text overflow. On Fairy Ring, the “follow her” prompt doesn't fit inside its box.

Double message. When buying and equipping, the message shows up twice and both overlap.

ModerateVery much in the priority list, affects the gameplay.

Hitbox not counting. The image and video show the box clearly touching an obstacle, but it didn't count as a hit.

MajorHighest priority, can make the game unplayable.

Sudden reset. On Fairy Ring the game told me to boost twice. I didn't, fell behind, and died while passing through a hole without touching any obstacle.

Passing through obstacles. On Fairy Ring the game told me to boost. I didn't, and still went straight through a closed obstacle.

Pip has no word filter. I typed a rude test phrase into Pip's message to check for word restrictions. There were none, so Pip can say anything.

💭 SuggestionsTwo new modes and three revamps

Additional game modes

High risk, high reward. On any map the player picks, their speed is doubled, and to make up for it they earn 1.5x more stars.

Mini boss fight. While going through the levels of a map, the body's immunity cells can wake up, follow the player and shoot a projectile once in a while. Why: these events either help players progress faster or add unpredictability.

Revamp

Control buttons. The power buttons have no names, so you have to look at them for a moment to know which is which. With names written on them, players can use them instinctively, because letters are easy to read from the corner of your eye.

Warning messages. Three warning messages show up for the same thing. Players don't know which to read first, fail to read properly and die.

Multiplayer. If another player is right beside you, they show up as a small circle far ahead. I suggest both players see each other as blocks, which gives a better and more competitive experience.

🥇 FTUETutorial, UI / UX and controls, graphics

Tutorial

Tutorial map. Very good, apart from the timing issue from my minor bugs.

Boss fight tips. Vague, and sometimes players can't see them because so many messages appear at once. On the Lungs I was told to go around the thread, and I was confused for a long time. Then I just tried not standing in front of it and didn't die. So “going around” only meant not being in front of the thread.

UI / UX / Controls

UI. Good, but there are many overlap bugs on mobile (see minor bugs).

UX. Gamepass prices and the skip and retry options are very tempting. Skip is just 13 Robux, which is a steal for p2w players.

Controls. Very good. Every movement command responds so fast it feels like being the Flash. The devs even added reduce motion and a cursor color option so players can progress more easily.

Graphics & animation

Looks. Peak. Especially the first stage of any map, where the transition happens, and the boss fights, which make my heart race.

🚀 PerformanceLag and overall bug count

Lagging. Occasional lag spikes and delays, caused by boss fights with a lot of graphics, device overheating, internet issues and so on. Not a big deal, since it never froze or crashed the game.

Bug encounters. A lot, but mostly minor. The few major bugs only happen under certain conditions.

📈 ProgressionHow long each map took me

Tutorial map, ~35 min. The easiest map I've played. Progression may look slow, but that's because I had a hard time adapting to the game.

Tornado, ~45 min. Not very challenging. Before, the rotation mechanic at level 6 was near impossible. It took some time to adapt, but I cleared it easily.

Fairy Ring, ~1h 30m. Levels 1 to 6 were easy. Level 7 rage-baited me for 30+ minutes because of the boost mechanic: the fairy switches position at the last moment and kills players who don't react in time.

Heart, ~2 hours. One of the hardest maps of all time. You travel through narrow space while dodging obstacles, and sometimes need very fast reactions to avoid obstacles that are extremely close.

Spine, not completed. The hardest game mode I've played. After an hour straight I wasn't even close to beating stage 1 of 8, because of the rotating map and close obstacles. It takes intense reaction speed and a clear head to not get confused by the rotation.

🎁 MiscellaneousShop, locker, multiplayer and workshop

Shop & locker. The locker is well made, you can choose what you want, like a different pip color or trail. The shop is a great addition: it gives better variants of the power you get at the start, and you can only buy them after reaching certain levels.

Multiplayer. Done great, and it can be improved a lot with the suggestion above, so players can see exactly how far or near the others are.

Workshop. One of the best additions. Players make their own maps and others test them. The problem is the lack of freedom, for example you can't make a very small map, which is annoying.

Publishing. I'm glad the developer has to clear their own map before posting, so there's no flood of troll maps.

😈 BossesThe Eye, Lungs, Fairy Ring, Heart

The Eye. The most balanced boss. Pip's tips are easy to follow and the attacks are easy to dodge. It took 4 to 5 tries at most.

The Lungs. Pretty difficult because of message overcrowding and confusing tips from Pip. It cost me around 20 minutes before I understood how to play it and beat it.

Fairy Ring. The cheap tricks are easy to see, but combined with the fast speed and the quick response needed to hit the fairy, it takes a split second to decide which is the real one, so players often die in this phase. In phase 2, the message on how to avoid the fairy when 2 tunnels appear is only shown briefly. I ignored it until I used time stop to read it and realized I have to bait the fairy to avoid getting caught.

Heart. One of the hardest boss fights I've faced. Defeat after defeat because of the “beating mechanism”: on every beat the player becomes fast for a short moment, which messes with your control over speed and reaction. Add close obstacles and narrow tunnels, and it's very hard.

❓ QuestionsDifficulty spike, where I got stuck, where I quit

Difficulty spike. After each map the next one is on another level, and the time to beat each map keeps growing. The jump is a bit too much for players. From Fairy Ring the bar was set a little too high, Heart was way above what normal players can reach, and Spine was impossible for players even after 100 to 150 attempts.

Where I got stuck: Spine stage 1. Even after 150+ attempts I couldn't clear it. The furthest I got was the 65% completion bar. The rotating map combined with close obstacles takes insane reaction speed and focus.

Where I quit: Fairy Ring boss. 150+ attempts and about an hour on the boss fight alone. Cheap tricks to avoid attacks, plus a boost mechanic that makes obstacles come much faster. And phase 2 makes you decide quickly during the tunnel phase, or the fairy catches you no matter what.

💪 AbilitiesTime stop, Boost, Pulse, Snap shot

Time stop. One of the best abilities. It gives players a brief moment to relax or assess the situation. The flaw is that it isn't instant, so you have to activate it early.

Boost. One of the best abilities, and also the one with the worst flaw. You get a lot of speed, but obstacles appear much faster than expected, so you need instant reactions. Most players hardly use it unless the game tells them to.

Pulse. The only ability with no downside, and any downside is covered by the Pulse variants in the shop.

Snap shot. I couldn't reach level 14. I got to about level 10 before giving up because the Spine map was too hard to clear.

✉️ FeedbackFinal thoughts

Balance. The game is made very well, but it needs a lot of rebalancing in map difficulty, like Fairy Ring, Heart, Spine and more.

Mobile. It isn't very compatible with mobile players, as shown by the overlap bugs and the difficulty of using the controls.

Potential. If these things are fixed properly, the game will definitely succeed. Its potential is easy to see.
